Quick notes from my side after a first pass on the CSV:

- The hourly peaks show sharp spikes (10–12x baseline) for ~30–45 minute promo bursts. That argues for some headroom or burst capacity rather than strictly overprovisioning for peak.
- For the prompt mix you described, assume avg tokens/request ~ 110 and avg tokens/response ~ 150 once you include system/context. If the creative 450-token class happens <10% of the time, we can treat those as backfill or route to a higher-capacity variant.
- If you require p95 < 250ms for responses up to 200 tokens, we should target p99 < 600ms for 450-token tails on the latency-optimized build.

Preliminary starter footprint (very conservative):
- Latency-optimal: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs with 10–12 concurrent sessions/GPU (low oversubscription), KV-cache enabled, int8 quantization on the medium-long model variant.
- Cost-optimal: 5x A10G-equivalent GPUs with 20–24 concurrent sessions/GPU (3–4x oversubscription), aggressive batching and prefix caching, mixed int8/int4 quantization.

Open questions I want Sam to confirm:
1) Embedding rate (percent of sessions that call vector DB).
2) Percent of sessions that maintain long conversation state (>15 messages) — impacts KV cache size.
3) Whether a cross-region failover (eu/us) is needed at launch.

I'll build a quick spreadsheet with throughput assumptions and cost delta and send in the next message.

—Ben
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial_starter_footprint_estimates.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)
